subject: SLA availability floor & p95 latency exception proposal — ClearStream
messages:
From: Emma Holden <emma.holden@clearstream.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearStream Procurement <procurement@clearstream.io>
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Service availability & latency exceptions for batched workloads

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — ClearStream’s infra and inference stack look promising. Procurement asked me to surface one sticking point before we move to legal: the SLA attachment in the standard Redwood template assumes a 99.9% monthly uptime floor and p95 latency by model/route. For our batched inference workload (nightly bulk scoring of ~10M rows), we expect higher tail latency and some controlled maintenance during the nightly window.

Specifically we are requesting:
- A temporary availability floor of 99.7% (instead of 99.9%) for the first 6 months while we ramp traffic and enable KV-prefix caching.
- An explicit carveout that allows up to two 3-hour nightly maintenance windows per week for heavy model refreshes (these should not trigger credits).
- A separate p95 latency objective for batched routes (we propose 400ms) while keeping real-time routes at 250ms.

Can Redwood accommodate these exception terms, and if so, how would monthly service credits be calculated for the batched route deviations? Procurement is sensitive to open-ended credit exposure.

If easier, I can loop in legal (we have DocuSign ready) but wanted to see if we can align commercial terms with you first.

Thanks — Emma

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Emma Holden <emma.holden@clearstream.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service availability & latency exceptions for batched workloads

Hi Emma — really appreciate the clear ask and the heads-up from Procurement. We can be flexible here; thanks for outlining the batch vs real-time split. A few early thoughts and a proposed starting point attached: redwood-credit-schedule.csv (editable).

High level proposal (we can wave these into the contract as an SLA Amendment):
1) Availability floor: 99.8% baseline for first 6 months (midpoint between our standard and your ask). If ClearStream hits >90% of committed monthly throughput we keep 99.8%; below that we revert to standard 99.9 baseline with pro-rata credits (this prevents free credits during low usage).
2) Nightly maintenance carveouts: allow up to two 3-hour nightly windows per week per region for heavy model refreshes. Maintenance notified >=72 hours and scheduled between 00:00–05:00 local region time will be excluded from credit calculations. Any unplanned downtime outside of these windows still counts toward uptime.
3) Latency: keep real-time p95 objective at 250ms; create a batched-route p95 objective at 400ms. Credits for latency miss on batched routes only apply after a sustained monthly exceedance (more than 3 separate daily incidents affecting >10% of batch jobs).
4) Credit calculation: for batched-route availability misses we propose a capped monthly credit = min( (monthly revenue * 0.02), $75k ) per month for the first 6 months; for repeated misses we will escalate to a joint remediation plan and revisit the cap. For latency misses on batched routes we propose service credits at a lower multiplier (0.5x) of the availability formula.

I attached a CSV that maps uptime bands -> credit % and a draft amendment PDF. If these look directionally right, Ben can join a sync with your procurement/legal to nail wording and DocuSign flow.

Short answer: yes, we can accommodate exception mechanics, but we prefer caps and conditional triggers tied to throughput and scheduled maintenance windows to limit open exposure.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das

From: Emma Holden <emma.holden@clearstream.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearStream Procurement <procurement@clearstream.io>
Date: 2027-04-06T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service availability & latency exceptions for batched workloads

Priyom — thanks for the quick reply and the draft. Procurement is generally comfortable with a capped exposure but has two asks before we proceed:

1) The 99.8% floor still feels like we (ClearStream) are shouldering the ramp risk. Would Redwood accept a 99.7% floor for the first 3 months (trial run) and then 99.8% for months 4–6 before moving to standard 99.9%? That reduces our early migration risk.
2) For the credit cap: can you clarify whether the $75k cap is per region or global per account? We operate EU + US and need regional carveouts.

Also legal redlined the maintenance notice clause — they want a shorter notification window for emergency model refreshes triggered by data quality incidents (48 hours). Is there an operational playbook we can reference for emergency updates? I uploaded our redlines here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-clearstream-sla-redlines

If Redwood can confirm regional caps and accept the 3-month initial floor at 99.7% we can route this to DocuSign today.

—Emma

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Emma Holden <emma.holden@clearstream.io>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Service availability & latency exceptions for batched workloads

Emma — appreciate the specificity. Internal recap for transparency: Priyom proposed 99.8% for 6 months, carveouts for scheduled nightly maintenance, and a capped credit schedule. ClearStream asked for a stepped approach (99.7% x3 months -> 99.8% x3 months -> 99.9%). Regional cap question and emergency notice callouts outstanding.

We can accept the stepped availability floor as you proposed (99.7% first 3 months, 99.8% months 4–6) subject to two operational guardrails:
- Regional cap: the $75k cap is per region (US/EU) for the first 6 months; if you add APAC it will be a separate cap tier.
- Emergency updates: we can shorten scheduled-notice for emergency model refreshes to 48 hours, provided ClearStream authorizes a designated ops contact list for emergency pushes. We'll add an emergency-runbook reference to the amendment (appendix B) that details rollback, verification, and monitoring steps.

As a commercial sweetener to get you live faster, Redwood will include a 3-month pilot commitment appendix: for months 1–3 availability measured under the 99.7% floor will have a reduced remedy multiplier (0.5x) for credits — this lets us limit initial financial exposure while we co-tune caching and batching. After month 3 we switch to the full credit multiplier at the stepped floors. I've attached the pilot appendix for review.

Next steps:
- If ClearStream signs off on regional caps and emergency-runbook contacts, we'll finalize the amendment and route to DocuSign (link will be shared by our legal ops).
- Priyom, please schedule a 30-minute call with ClearStream procurement + ops tomorrow to capture contacts and finalize the appendices.

Emma — can you confirm the two points and the preferred time for the call?

Best — Ben
